question.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the manic episode

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.

subtypes.Racing Thoughts: Thoughts spinning too fast in the head, constantly jumping from one idea to another.
subtypes.Flooding of Thoughts: Too many thoughts emerging simultaneously, making them disorganized.
subtypes.Inability to Control Thoughts: Unable to stop or slow down thoughts and unable to calm the mind.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

info.persona: Joseph Holmes is a curiosity-driven sales strategist who can’t resist a craft-beer sampler after a long week, yet they habitually forget to water houseplants until the weekend.
info.professional_persona: Joseph Holmes is a 26-year-old sales professional who leverages data-driven market research and a flair for persuasive storytelling to build long-term wholesale partnerships, while they infuse their creative curiosity into innovative sales strategies.
info.cultural_background: Joseph was raised in Providence, Rhode Island, in a working‑class family with deep roots in the region. While his ethnic background is white, his community is a mosaic of Irish, Italian, and Portuguese heritage, exposing him to a blend of traditions such as local seafood cuisine, seasonal festivals, and a strong sense of community solidarity. The New England work ethic and the bustling waterfront commerce of Providence have shaped his practical, down‑to‑earth outlook, while the city's vibrant arts scene nurtured his appreciation for creative expression. He identifies with the modest, community‑oriented values of the area and stays connected through local events, neighborhood gatherings, and support for local artisans.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Joseph's free time reflects his social and artistic side. He frequents Providence's galleries and museums, often sketching street art and attending opening nights. He plays in an intramural soccer league and organizes weekend hikes along the Rhode Island coastline, enjoying the area's natural scenery. He is a regular at local craft‑brew festivals, experiments with cooking seafood dishes, and volunteers as a mentor for youth art programs at a community center. He also enjoys exploring new music venues and reading books on design and emerging technologies.
info.sports_persona: Joseph Holmes plays in an intramural soccer league on Saturdays, follows the Boston Red Sox during baseball season and the New England Patriots in the fall, and they stay fit by jogging along the Providence waterfront and attending weekly training sessions with the Rhode Island Coastal Hikers club.
info.arts_persona: Joseph Holmes frequents Providence’s contemporary art galleries, often sketching the bold murals inspired by artists such as Banksy and local muralist Peter Gunter, while they unwind at music venues that showcase the atmospheric sounds of The Mighty Mighty Bosstones and indie folk singer Brandi Carlile.
info.travel_persona: Joseph Holmes prefers spontaneous weekend getaways, often packing a bike for a quick ride to Block Island or a ferry trip to Martha’s Vineyard, while they dream of a future European surf road trip along Portugal’s Algarve coast after saving enough for a longer adventure.
info.culinary_persona: Joseph Holmes, a confident home cook, loves preparing fresh Rhode Island clam chowder with potatoes, thyme, and locally sourced clams, and they often experiment with grilled lobster rolls seasoned with clarified butter, lemon zest, and a pinch of Old Bay.

info.persona: Yanira Ramos blends disciplined cash‑handling expertise with a relaxed, curiosity‑driven outlook, savoring spicy home‑cooked meals, hustling toward retail leadership, yet they openly admit to occasional disorganization and impulse kitchen‑gadget purchases.
info.professional_persona: Yanira Ramos, a veteran cashier renowned for flawless cash reconciliation and bilingual (Spanish‑English) rapport, turns her calm, resilient demeanor and competitive streak into a knack for spotting inventory gaps and upselling, even as they embrace a relaxed, occasionally disorganized work style while eyeing a shift‑supervisor promotion.
info.cultural_background: Yanira was raised in a Mexican‑American household in Dallas, the daughter of immigrants who emphasized family, hard work, and cultural pride. Bilingual from childhood, she seamlessly switches between Spanish and English, preserving Mexican traditions while navigating mainstream American life. Community events, spicy home‑cooked meals, and stories of her heritage shape her identity. Her cultural background instills a pragmatic outlook, strong resilience, and a deep appreciation for the vibrant Mexican community that thrives throughout Texas, influencing both her personal values and professional ethos.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her downtime, Yanira enjoys cooking traditional Mexican dishes, experimenting with regional recipes she learned from her family. She frequently explores Dallas’s vibrant food‑truck scene and visits local farmer’s markets for fresh ingredients. Yanira attends cultural celebrations such as Cinco de Mayo and Día de los Muertos, appreciating the community connection. She reads entrepreneurial and self‑improvement books to satisfy her curiosity, and unwinds with true‑crime podcasts. Outdoor activities like hiking the Cedar Ridge trail provide balance, while occasional yoga sessions help maintain her calm resilience. She also dabbles in DIY home‑decor projects and plays beginner guitar as a creative outlet.
info.sports_persona: Yanira Ramos, a devoted supporter of the Dallas Cowboys, Dallas Mavericks, and Texas Rangers, combines her love of competition with community by joining the Dallas Hiking Club for weekly Cedar Ridge Trail treks, attending beginner yoga sessions at a local studio, and playing in a co‑ed recreational soccer league, while they maintain a balanced fitness routine.
info.arts_persona: Yanira Ramos, who immerses herself in the vibrant works of Frida Kahlo and the soulful melodies of Selena, regularly visits the Dallas Museum of Art’s Latin American exhibit, streams concerts by Los Tigres del Norte, and practices beginner guitar with folk songs, allowing artistic appreciation to color their leisure.
info.travel_persona: Yanira Ramos, who prefers spontaneous weekend getaways over rigid itineraries, has road‑tripped to Oaxaca to explore regional cuisine, spent a long weekend in New Orleans for its music scene, and dreams of hiking the Sonoran Desert, while they balance travel costs with modest savings and occasional family responsibilities.
info.culinary_persona: Yanira Ramos, an intermediate home chef specializing in corn‑tortilla based dishes like chilaquiles, mole verde, and carnitas, sources fresh chilies, epazote, and queso fresco from Dallas farmer’s markets, enjoys experimenting with regional sauces, and often indulges in food‑truck tacos, while they occasionally order fast‑food for convenience despite their love for cooking.

info.persona: Garrett Tasker, a 41‑year‑old psychologist who fuses art and science, hikes, paints, and strums folk tunes while balancing a disciplined finance plan, modest health quirks, and an insatiable curiosity that fuels both professional ambition and weekend passions.
info.professional_persona: Garrett Tasker, a licensed psychologist specializing in cognitive‑behavioral therapy, psychometric assessment, and group facilitation, merges rigorous data‑driven analysis with inventive art‑therapy techniques, channeling their critical yet open mindset into pioneering treatment programs while mentoring junior clinicians.
info.cultural_background: Garrett grew up in the Lehigh Valley of Pennsylvania within a predominantly white, middle‑class American environment that values education, community involvement, and modest regional traditions such as local fairs and Pennsylvania Dutch heritage. His family emphasized liberal arts studies, fostering an open‑minded, curiosity‑driven outlook while maintaining practical responsibility. The blend of suburban familiarity and exposure to nearby cultural hubs like Philadelphia and New York nurtured his appreciation for the arts and critical thinking. This cultural backdrop shapes his professional ethos of combining rigorous scientific practice with creative, unconventional approaches.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Garrett is an avid art enthusiast who frequently visits regional galleries and creates acrylic paintings in his home studio. He enjoys hiking the Appalachian trails around Pennsylvania, often combining physical activity with reflective journaling. Playing acoustic guitar and exploring folk music give him an outlet for social gatherings and informal performances. His intellectual curiosity leads him to read contemporary philosophy, literary fiction, and cutting‑edge psychology research. He volunteers at local mental‑health nonprofits, participates in community theater productions, and travels to culturally rich cities to experience diverse artistic traditions.
info.sports_persona: Garrett Tasker, a devoted Appalachian Trail hiker and occasional pickup basketball player, follows a weekly routine of long treks supplemented by yoga stretches, roots for the Philadelphia Eagles in the fall and the Pittsburgh Penguins during winter, and actively participates in the Pennsylvania Appalachian Trail Club’s weekend outings.
info.arts_persona: Garrett Tasker, an avid gallery visitor and amateur acrylic painter, draws inspiration from Georgia O'Keeffe and Mark Rothko, frequents the Philadelphia Museum of Art and local Cornwall Art Center, and brings folk songs by Bob Dylan and Joni Mitchell to life on acoustic guitar during community theater gatherings.
info.travel_persona: Garrett Tasker, who craves culturally immersive experiences, crafts itineraries that blend museum visits in Paris, street‑art tours in Berlin, and weekend hikes in the Blue Ridge Mountains, preferring boutique hostels and integrating volunteer mental‑health workshops whenever possible.
info.culinary_persona: Garrett Tasker, a competent home cook, favors Mediterranean‑style meals such as grilled salmon with quinoa and roasted vegetables, delights in homemade pesto and seasonal pumpkin soup, and tops off evenings with a handcrafted espresso sweetened with lavender‑infused honey after painting sessions.
